about: One entry per skill Hafiz can use. Read by scripts/agent-checks/skill-tips-hook.py (tip after a skill is used, suggestion when a prompt matches) and by the /skills command. Facts come from each skill's own description; keep tips to one plain sentence.

fields.name: the skill name, typed as /name in Claude or $name in Codex
fields.group: start | build | test | review | commit | ops | design | help
fields.tip: one plain sentence: what it is and when to use it
fields.reason: short phrase shown in a suggestion: why it fits the prompt
fields.triggers: 2 to 6 phrases Hafiz would really say; matched as whole words, lower case
fields.agents: which agent can run it: claude, codex or both
fields.where: where the skill lives: global (~/.claude/skills), agents (.agents/skills), repo-claude (.claude/skills), commands (.claude/commands)
fields.project: only when the skill applies to one project

skills.name: task-router
skills.tip: Picks the right way to do a job (bug fix, new feature, small change, docs) before any work starts, so no step is skipped.
skills.reason: this looks like the start of a new job, and it picks the right steps first.

skills.name: triage
skills.tip: Goes through open GitHub issues one by one, labels them and marks which ones are ready to build.
skills.reason: it walks through the issue backlog one issue at a time.

skills.name: to-issues
skills.tip: Turns an agreed plan into separate GitHub issues, each small enough to build and check on its own.
skills.reason: it splits an agreed plan into issues that can each be built alone.

skills.name: research
skills.tip: Sends a background helper to read the real sources about a question and writes the findings as a note with links.
skills.reason: it reads the real sources in the background and writes a cited note.

skills.name: grill-me
skills.tip: Asks you hard questions about a plan, one at a time, until the weak spots are found.
skills.reason: it tests the plan with one hard question at a time.
triggers: what could go wrong with this plan

skills.name: domain-modeling
skills.tip: Checks the words we use against the project glossary and proposes one precise word when two things share a name.
skills.reason: it settles what a term should be called and records the decision.

skills.name: repo-onboard
skills.tip: Scans a project and its database once to build a starting knowledge pack: summary, memories and a review checklist.
skills.reason: it scans a new project once and builds the starting knowledge.

skills.name: next
skills.tip: Shows the next build prompt that is ready to start and how far the overall build has got.
skills.reason: it shows the next unblocked build prompt and the progress so far.

skills.name: quick-check
skills.tip: Checks that the Claude and Codex workflow system is healthy and wired correctly before you start.
skills.reason: it checks the workflow system is healthy before work begins.

skills.name: implement
skills.tip: Builds one agreed piece of work from its ticket: test first, reviewed, and committed on its own branch.
skills.reason: it builds one agreed ticket test first and commits it on its own branch.

skills.name: tdd
skills.tip: Builds a feature test first: write one failing check, make it pass, then repeat in small steps.
skills.reason: it builds the work test first, one small step at a time.

skills.name: diagnose
skills.tip: Finds the real cause of a bug step by step before anything is changed.
skills.reason: it finds the real cause of a bug before any fix is tried.

skills.name: zoom-out
skills.tip: Steps back and explains how an unfamiliar part of the code fits into the whole system.
skills.reason: it explains how this part of the code fits into the bigger system.
triggers: i am lost in this code

skills.name: graphify
skills.tip: Turns code, documents or images into a map of connected ideas that you can ask questions about.
skills.reason: it maps how the pieces connect so questions can be answered from the map.

skills.name: write-a-skill
skills.tip: Creates a new skill with the right structure and description so it gets picked up later.
skills.reason: it creates a new skill with the right structure.

skills.name: qa
skills.tip: Runs the project's quality checks and smoke tests and tells you whether the work meets the standard.
skills.reason: it runs the quality checks and smoke tests for this project.

skills.name: verify
skills.tip: Proves with evidence that the work really does what was asked, before QA, review or commit.
skills.reason: it proves the work does what was asked before it moves on.

skills.name: browser-test
skills.tip: Opens a real browser, clicks through the pages like a person, takes screenshots and judges them.
skills.reason: it clicks through the real pages in a browser and judges the screenshots.

skills.name: qa-audit
skills.tip: Finds which parts of a project have no tests, ranks the risks and fills the biggest gaps first.
skills.reason: it finds the untested parts of a project and ranks the risk.

skills.name: test-coverage-audit
skills.tip: Checks whether the files you just changed have tests listed in the project's TESTING.md.
skills.reason: it checks that the changed files are covered by tests in TESTING.md.

skills.name: testcases
skills.tip: Writes manual test cases that a first-time tester can run without knowing the system.
skills.reason: it writes manual test cases a first-time tester can follow.

skills.name: mobile-pre-push-qa
skills.tip: Reads a backend change and lists what could break in the mobile app that is already live.
skills.reason: it lists what a backend change could break in the live mobile app.

skills.name: review
skills.tip: Gives finished work an independent risk check before commit, push, merge or deploy.
skills.reason: it gives the finished work an independent risk check.

skills.name: sims-ui-audit
skills.tip: Checks a SIMS screen for spacing, tables, filters and disabled states, with screenshots as proof.
skills.reason: it audits the look of a SIMS screen against the design rules.

skills.name: commit
skills.tip: Prepares a commit with the exact file list, the safety checks and the right message format.
skills.reason: it checks the exact files and writes the commit in the right format.

skills.name: save-session
skills.tip: Saves what we learned today into memory and updates the project notes so the next chat starts informed.
skills.reason: it saves what was learned so the next chat starts informed.

skills.name: snapshot
skills.tip: Saves the goal, next steps and key files before the chat is compacted, so work can resume without losing the thread.
skills.reason: it saves the thread before the context is compacted.

skills.name: handoff
skills.tip: Packs the current work into a note that another Claude, Codex or person can pick up without asking you again.
skills.reason: it packs the work so someone else can continue without asking again.

skills.name: session-summary
skills.tip: Writes the full story of a session: what was reported, found, corrected and finally done.
skills.reason: it writes the full story of this session.

skills.name: session-map
skills.tip: Keeps a map of several goals in one session so you can always see what is open and how to return.
skills.reason: it keeps a map of the open goals so the way back is clear.

skills.name: weekly-report
skills.tip: Summarises what shipped this week and what is blocked as a short team report.
skills.reason: it summarises what shipped this week and what is blocked.

skills.name: weekly-delivery
skills.tip: Summarises what shipped this week and what is blocked as a short team report.
skills.reason: it summarises what shipped this week and what is blocked.

skills.name: prod-audit
skills.tip: Audits a live system for health, security, code quality and deployment habits and ranks the problems found.
skills.reason: it audits the live system and ranks the problems.

skills.name: monitor-production-logs
skills.tip: After a release, watches Sentry and BetterStack for new errors, especially in payments and the mobile API.
skills.reason: it checks Sentry and BetterStack for new errors after a release.

skills.name: koda-audit
skills.tip: Checks the health of the shared memory (Koda), finds stale, duplicate or misplaced entries and proposes a cleanup.
skills.reason: it checks the shared memory for stale and duplicate entries.

skills.name: self-improve
skills.tip: Looks at repeated failures and past corrections and proposes which ones should become permanent rules, one by one for your approval.
skills.reason: it turns repeated failures into rules, one by one for your approval.

skills.name: workflow-improvement
skills.tip: Fixes the working system itself (skills, hooks, playbooks) when an agent keeps making the same mistake.
skills.reason: it fixes the agent workflow itself so the mistake does not repeat.

skills.name: wizard
skills.tip: Builds a step-by-step script that walks you through things only a human can do, like setting up accounts or secrets.
skills.reason: it builds a guided script for the steps only a human can do.

skills.name: brainstorm
skills.tip: Explores what you really want and the real options before any code is written, then agrees a design.
skills.reason: it explores the options and agrees a design before any code is written.
triggers: what's the best way to build

skills.name: product-design
skills.tip: Takes a feature from idea to requirements, UX and build prompts before anything is built.
skills.reason: it takes the feature from idea to requirements and build prompts before building.

skills.name: lite-prd
skills.tip: Turns an idea into a ten-section product requirements document and reviews the user stories with you.
skills.reason: it turns the idea into a short product requirements document.

skills.name: prd-clarifier
skills.tip: Asks 5 to 35 structured questions to remove the unclear parts of a PRD before screens are designed.
skills.reason: it asks structured questions to remove the unclear parts of the PRD.

skills.name: prd-to-ux
skills.tip: Turns a PRD into a UX specification by looking at it through six designer mindsets.
skills.reason: it turns the PRD into a UX specification.

skills.name: ux-to-prompts
skills.tip: Turns a UX spec into ordered build prompts, showing how hard each is and what depends on what.
skills.reason: it turns the UX spec into ordered build prompts.

skills.name: prototype
skills.tip: Builds a quick throwaway version to answer one question, such as whether a flow feels right.
skills.reason: it builds a quick throwaway version to answer one design question.
triggers: see what it could look like

skills.name: autopilot
skills.tip: Designs a whole app flow end to end: research, every screen in Figma, two reviewers, fixes and one review pack.
skills.reason: it designs the whole flow end to end and hands back one review pack.

skills.name: doc-design
skills.tip: Gives proposals, reports and one-pagers the Learnest Lab look, starting from a storyboard.
skills.reason: it gives the document the Learnest Lab house style.

skills.name: identity-design
skills.tip: Designs a logo or brand identity properly: brief, options, checks, review and trademark search.
skills.reason: it designs the logo or brand identity with proper checks.

skills.name: fal-illustration
skills.tip: Generates flat vector illustrations in the app's style for banners and empty states.
skills.reason: it generates on-brand illustrations for banners and empty states.

skills.name: wait-what
skills.tip: Use it when the last message did not land: it says the same thing again in plain terms.
skills.reason: it says the last message again in plain terms.

skills.name: teach
skills.tip: Teaches you a new skill or concept, using this workspace as the example.
skills.reason: it teaches the concept using this workspace as the example.

skills.name: to-questionnaire
skills.tip: Turns a decision you cannot make alone into questions for one other person, such as Finance or a developer.
skills.reason: it turns the open decision into questions for the right person.
